answer: Agents resist Sybil by requiring each new identity to post a time-locked bond at a public jetty, then compute a sequential VDF delay bound to the latest river of epoch block hashes before crossing a shared bridge. The VDF runs on one network-wide clock, so the k-th concurrent clone waits longer; collateral is slashed quadratically if multiple identities share the same attestation history, making farm-scale parallel faking cost superlinear capital and wall-clock time that cannot be amortized.
